title: Adaptive sidebar zoning and task-flow mapping for Console navigation
creator: Marin Alvarez
description: Goal: redefine Console navigation to support task-oriented flows (dashboards, rollouts, cost views) while making workspace switching and deep links predictable. We propose an adaptive sidebar zoning pattern that separates: 1) persistent primary actions (Workspaces, Search, Home), 2) context modules (Models, Deployments, Billing) and 3) ephemeral tools (Notifications, Quick Actions). The sidebar collapses into compact mode with a focused quick-open command palette and preserves deep links so existing bookmarks continue to work. This ticket covers IA diagrams, high-fidelity prototypes, engineering constraints, and a migration plan for legacy routes.
acceptance_criteria: Zoned sidebar prototype built in Figma with desktop + narrow widths
Navigational test: representative user completes common tasks (create rollout, view cost breakdown, open workspace) within 3 clicks on average
Deep links to dashboards and rollout detail pages remain stable and resolve across workspace context
Console telemetry emits route-change events and workspace-scoped tags for every primary nav click
Accessibility: keyboard navigation and screen reader labels pass basic a11y audit
decisions: Adopt 3-zone sidebar (Persistent / Context / Tools) with an optional compact mode
Keep workspace switcher anchored to the top of the sidebar for discoverability; also expose a global quick-switcher (Cmd+K) that ignores zoning
Route model: URL pattern /workspace/:wid/(zone)/(resource)/:id to make deep linking explicit and allow routing middleware to rehydrate workspace state
Defer multi-tenant RBAC UI changes to a follow-up ticket to limit scope
Engineering requested a rollback-safe feature flag and runtime guard for legacy route redirects
prototypes: Clickable flow for workspace-switch + create-rollout: https://www.figma.com/proto/AdaptiveFlow
